title: Oil Surges Past $97 as Hormuz Tension Lifts Energy Stocks
summary: Brent crude tops $97 a barrel as Strait of Hormuz tension escalates. Energy leads the S&P 500 while the broader market trades cautiously.
body_markdown:
Gotrade News - Global oil prices surged to multi-month highs, with Brent crude trading near $97.5 a barrel on Tuesday, September 8. According to[Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil) , Brent is up more than 11% over the past month and nearly 47% over the past year.


The rally is driven by renewed tension in the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most strategic oil shipping lane. As reported by[Bloomberg Technoz](https://www.bloombergtechnoz.com/detail-news/120818/harga-minyak-naik-saat-pakta-iran-oman-soal-hormuz-kian-dekat) , crude has climbed more than 30% since the conflict erupted in late February.


## Key Takeaways


- Brent is near $97.5 and WTI above $92 a barrel on supply-risk fears tied to the Strait of Hormuz.
- Energy was the strongest sector in the S&P 500, while the broader market traded cautiously.
- Iran says a safe-passage pact with Oman has reached its final stage, a catalyst investors should watch this week.


Tensions escalated after the US struck Iranian oil tankers, raising fears of prolonged supply disruptions. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, as quoted by Bloomberg Technoz, said roughly 8 million barrels of oil per day flow out of the Persian Gulf through the strait.
